topic: Grover's Algorithm: The Quantum Search Engine
target_audience: University students with basic linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Classical Search Dilemma
lecture_lines: Searching unstructured databases is a common challenge.
For N items, we check each one sequentially.
Classically, finding a target takes O(N) steps.
animations: Create a 10x10 grid of 100 white (#FFFFFF) squares representing boxes.
Animate a yellow (#FFFF00) border moving sequentially through the first 50 squares.
Display text 'Classical Search: O(N) complexity' in white (#FFFFFF) at the bottom.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Quantum Superposition
lecture_lines: Quantum computers use superposition to check items simultaneously.
We represent every possibility with equal probability amplitudes.
All states start in a uniform flat sea.
animations: Morph the grid of squares into a bar chart with 100 thin blue (#5271FF) bars of equal height.
Draw a dashed cyan (#00FFFF) horizontal line across the tops of all bars.
Display label 'Quantum Superposition: All states exist simultaneously' in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (The Negative Flip)
lecture_lines: The Oracle identifies the correct answer among possibilities.
It flips the phase of the target state specifically.
Mathematically, it multiplies target amplitude by negative one.
The target bar flips below the horizontal axis.
All other amplitudes remain unchanged and upright.
animations: Identify the target bar at index 42 and change its color to orange (#FF8C00).
Show the label 'Oracle (U_w)' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oracle.svg] above the chart.
Animate the orange bar flipping vertically to point downwards (negative amplitude).
Show the dashed cyan (#00FFFF) average line shifting slightly downwards.
Pulse the orange bar to emphasize its phase flip.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Amplitude Amplification)
lecture_lines: We calculate the average height of all amplitudes.
Every wave reflects across this average line.
The flipped target state is pushed significantly higher.
Remaining non-target amplitudes shrink in the process.
This makes the correct answer stand out clearly.
animations: Show all bars and the cyan (#00FFFF) average line clearly.
Animate every bar reflecting across the average line: 'Height_new = 2*Average - Height_old'.
The negative orange bar shoots up, becoming much taller than the others.
The other blue bars shrink toward the zero-axis.
Display text 'Amplitude Amplification: Target stands out' in yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: The State Rotation
lecture_lines: Grover's algorithm performs a rotation in vector space.
The state moves from uncertainty toward the target.
Each iteration brings the vector closer to solution.
We need roughly square root of N rotations.
This geometric shift leads to the final measurement.
animations: Draw two perpendicular axes labeled |w> (vertical) and |s_perp> (horizontal) in white (#FFFFFF).
Draw a state vector (blue #5271FF) starting very close to the horizontal axis.
Rotate the vector toward the vertical axis by an angle of 2*theta.
Repeat the rotation animation to show the vector approaching the vertical axis.
Highlight the final vector and label the angle as 'sqrt(N) iterations' in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Conclusion: The Quadratic Speedup
lecture_lines: Grover's Algorithm provides a powerful quadratic speedup.
One million items searched in one thousand steps.
Quantum search is more efficient than classical methods.
animations: Display a comparison: 'Classical: 500,000 steps' vs 'Grover: 1,000 steps' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show the target bar probability reaching nearly 100% (height 1.0).
Fade in text 'Pixel found with high probability!' in green (#00FF00) accompanied by the pixel icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg].
